title: Prescriptive SDK error surface: human-readable codes, actionable guidance, and streaming fallback signals
creator: Leah Morgan
description:
Problem: SDK consumers across Python, TypeScript, and Go are getting opaque runtime errors from the runtime and network layers. Current SDKs surface low-level messages that are hard to map to concrete remediation steps (retry, backoff, switch to smaller context, use a different model variant, resume stream). This leads to poor DX, increased support burden, and customer-facing incidents where apps keep retrying incorrectly or drop streams without recovery.

Goal: Define and implement a prescriptive error surface across SDKs that provides: (1) stable error codes (string identifiers) that map to runbookable actions, (2) short actionable messages for developers, (3) machine-readable retry/backoff/resume hints, and (4) explicit streaming fallback signals (resume token semantics and when to fall back to polling or alternate model). The surface should be language-idiomatic (exceptions in Python, Error subclasses in TS, typed errors in Go) while maintaining a shared canonical mapping and telemetry semantics.

Scope: API/SDK layer only (Python, TypeScript, Go). Does not include runtime/kernel changes, but will include small server-side header conventions for hint metadata. Deliverables: spec document, cross-SDK reference implementation, test harness, migration guide, and public changelog/SDK docs.

Risks: Backwards compatibility for existing integrations; differences in language exception ergonomics; ensuring telemetry (error_code) tags are emitted consistently to tracing/metrics.

Out of scope: Changing HTTP status codes, global server retry policies, or user-facing CLI tooling.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical error-code registry (CSV) exists with <= 40 entries covering network, auth, model, quota, and streaming conditions
Each SDK exposes language-idiomatic error objects that include: code, brief_message, detailed_hint, retryable(boolean), recommended_backoff(string), resume_token(optional string)
Streaming clients expose a resumable stream API that surfaces a resume_token when available and a well-documented fallback path when not
Automated tests: cross-language test harness verifies mapping for 30+ simulated failure scenarios and ensures telemetry tag 'redwood.error_code' is set
Docs and migration guide published in docs.redwood.ai and linked from SDK release notes
No behavior changes for default retry semantics unless consumers opt into new retry_hint handling
plan: Phase 1: Spec and registry (2 weeks) -> produce canonical CSV and spec, internal review. Phase 2: SDK prototypes (3 weeks) -> implement error types in Python/TS/Go, add unit tests and example snippets. Phase 3: Streaming ergonomics (2 weeks) -> add resume_token handling and recommended fallback patterns. Phase 4: Cross-language test harness and trace verification (1 week). Phase 5: Docs, migration guide, and release (1 week).
